item.title: Blue Zones: Lifestyle Keys to Longevity NEW — Wed Nov 18, 1:00 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Register here.
What can we learn from the people who live the longest? This interactive program will introduce participants to Blue Zones, regions of the world that have been recognized for having unusually high numbers of people who live to very old ages. We will explore the lifestyle habits and daily practices of centenarians and consider how these lessons might be adapted to our own lives and communities.
The program will begin with a presentation introducing the concept of Blue Zones, including an overview of several Blue Zone regions around the world. The instructor will also share insights and experiences from a recent visit to Sardinia, Italy, one of the regions associated with longevity and a Blue Zone.

item.title: Writing: Method & Motivation — Wed Nov 18, 6:15 PM — Montclair Main - Conference Room
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
A workshop for anyone who wants to write or wants to infuse their existing writing practice with new energy. In each class, we'll consider one element of fiction or creative non-fiction, such as point of view, narrative voice, and what makes a piece of writing riveting, or boring. Students can expect in-class writing prompts, reading aloud, and optional homework. Positive encouragement, rather than formal critiques, will be featured, and inspiration and organization for writers will be discussed. Students should bring whatever they use to write to each class.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Ink and Insight: Writing for Mental Health and Happiness — Thu Nov 19, 2:00 PM — Montclair Main - Tower Room
item.description:
Journaling is an incredible tool for nurturing mental health and finding happiness. It allows us to reduce stress, release emotions, build mindfulness, and gain self-awareness—especially when it comes to identifying unhealthy patterns or habits. There are countless ways to approach journaling, each offering its own unique benefits to support better mental well-being.
In this two-session workshop, we’ll explore various journaling methods and delve into the specific advantages of each. Together, we’ll even dedicate time to put pen to paper and experience the therapeutic power of journaling firsthand.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Spiritual Enrichment Group: — Mon Feb 15, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Our Spiritual Enrichment Group is now meeting on the third Monday of the month at 7pm via Zoom. For many years we met at 11:45am (originally in-person and since the pandemic) via Zoom. In Spring 2026, Reverend Katherine sent the following message to our Church lay leaders: "Coffee hour is growing and newcomers are still walking through our doors. It is the only time that clergy has an opportunity to interact and be available to the congregation. Hanging around during clean up is a further opportunity as well. Exiting into an office with a closed door does not seem appropriate anymore."And so, members of the Spiritual Enrichment Group agreed to try meeting on Monday evenings; we use the Sunday Morning Worship Zoom Link. In certain seasons, we'll host a more regular (weekly) gathering using an agreed upon program. If you have any questions, speak with Reverend Katherine.
Source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona

item.title: Gemini Notebook: your AI research assistant — Wed Nov 18, 10:00 AM — Montclair campus - Sprague Library #203
item.description:
Discover how source-grounded AI differs from LLMs like, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini In this brief introduction to Gemini Notebook, you’ll learn how to upload a variety of sources, analyze dense scholarly articles, and chat directly with your personal research. It uses your exact source citations, thus reducing those troublesome AI hallucinations. We'll also explore the Studio to turn your Notebook into: study tools, detailed reports, beautiful slide presentations, infographics and videos. Gemini Notebook can also aggregate, cross reference, extract data and identify key findings from your uploaded sources. Register Here: https://montclair.libcal.com/event/18024894
Hosted by: Sprague Library
Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12982239
Source: Montclair State University

item.title: Rethinking Thanksgiving Through Food Sovereignty — Wed Nov 18, 11:45 AM — Schmitt Hall
item.description:
Join the New Jersey Center for Indigenous Justice for a discussion on our relationship to food, farming, and each other. item.title: The Party Scene - FREE Tickets for Students — Sun Nov 22, 3:00 PM — Kasser Theater
item.description:
The Hands Free & Dance Heginbotham: The Party Scene
Sun., November 22 @ 3PM
Exquisitely eclectic quartet The Hands Free and members of the fabulously whimsical Dance Heginbotham join forces in The Party Scene. Inspired by The Nutcracker and your holiday office party, this music and dance extravaganza is part Drosselmeyer and part Turkey Lurkey Time. Lightly immersive and family friendly, The Party Scene features student party guests from Montclair State University. All guests are encouraged to don impressively festive seasonal sweaters. About The Hands Free: The Hands Free is an acoustic quartet, bringing together the creative voices of composer/performers James Moore (guitar & banjo), Caroline Shaw (violin), Nathan Koci (accordion), and Eleonore Oppenheim (bass). Drawing from an eclectic array of influences in classical, jazz and folk traditions, the group produces a unique and evocative blend of joyful melodies, lush sonic textures and explosive improvisations.
